name: South Luangwa National Park
story: South Luangwa National Park covers 9,050 km2 in eastern Zambia. Founded as a game reserve in 1938 and becoming a national park in 1972, it sits in the valley of the meandering Luangwa River. The park supports over 400 bird species and more than 60 mammal species.
matters: The park spans woodland savannah eco-regions and includes the Nsefu Sector, supporting stable populations of lions, spotted hyenas, African wild dogs, and high densities of leopards.
